text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt the **Claude Self-Improvement Skill Pack** to automate prompt tuning and routing. It’s the fastest way to reduce manual review cycles while improving consistency—trade-off is initial setup time and dependency on the skill pack’s reliability. The alternative, manual tuning, scales poorly and risks human error.

name: Gauge
text: The Skill Pack’s reliability isn’t guaranteed—Cerebras’ model IDs just failed, so why trust another black box? A safer path is to fork the Skill Pack, audit the prompts/engines, and run a 5% canary with strict rollback triggers; settle the argument by proving the fork’s failure rate is below 1% in staging for a week.

name: Sprocket
text:
Adopt the **forked and audited Claude Self-Improvement Skill Pack** with a **5% canary deployment**. The fork lets us verify the prompts and routing logic before trusting it, while the canary limits blast radius if the fork fails. Trade-off: we delay full deployment by the time needed to audit and run the canary, but we avoid betting the system on an unproven black box.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-8199, worker-2638 — done, dissolved]

name: Gauge
text: The forked Skill Pack still carries the same risk of prompt failure—auditing doesn’t eliminate the 5% canary’s reputational damage if a broken prompt hits real users. A better alternative is to run the original Skill Pack behind a feature flag with strict rollback triggers, measuring failure rate against a 1% threshold for 48 hours before expanding; if it fails, we cut losses immediately and revisit the design. That settles the argument by proving the risk is manageable or forcing a pivot.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Fork the Claude Self-Improvement Skill Pack, audit its prompts/engines, then run a 0.1% canary for 48 hours with dual-prompt A/B logging and SLA—if failure rate stays below 1%, escalate to 1% for another 48 hours before full rollout.

Result: Forked artifact exists with audit trail and canary metrics; failure rates logged and SLA met.
Owner: Gauge.
